definition: The compact classical speech features derived from mel spectra.
details: The compact classical speech features derived from mel spectra. Dominated pre-deep-learning ASR; now mostly replaced by raw mel filterbanks or learned features, but still common in lightweight and embedded systems.

explainer.lead: MFCCs are compact classical speech features derived from mel spectra. They mattered because they dominated pre-deep-learning ASR, and they remain common in lightweight and embedded systems.

tiers.eli5: They are a short summary of how a chunk of speech sounds, small enough for tiny devices to handle.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers still use MFCCs where compute or memory is tight, such as embedded speech systems. A pitfall is assuming they are still the default: modern ASR mostly uses raw mel filterbanks or learned features instead.
tiers.paperLevel: Compact features computed from mel spectra, classically used as the input representation for ASR. They dominated pre-deep-learning ASR but have largely been replaced by raw mel filterbanks or learned features, except in lightweight and embedded settings.

explainer.example: An embedded speech recognizer extracts MFCCs from the audio as a compact feature representation instead of using learned features.
